attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing Yang-Mills input is a signed, scale-stable computation or bound for Lambda_-(K_v^sing) and for the OPE tail constant C_4 in the heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulator.
steps: Start from the post-H,K quotient block, where only the connected second boundary-OPE polarization remains in the Schur-Feshbach null scalar.
Expand each heat-kernel plaquette-sheet Wilson observable to four endpoint flux insertions using the same parallel transports used in the regulated Wilson loop.
Separate Wick-square contractions; they form a positive Gram matrix and therefore cannot be the negative endpoint falsifier.

Contract the local nonabelian commutator term proportional to C_A f f with the null incidence density. On straight shared segments the signed incidence sum is zero, so this contact cancels before any endpoint estimate is needed.

Partition the boundary footprint into endpoint boxes and straight interior pieces. The straight interior remainder has vanishing zeroth incidence moment, so the OPE Holder remainder gives T_tail <= C_4||u||_1^2(rho/ell_min)^eta.
Inside each endpoint box the remaining irreducible singlet four-flux cumulant is a finite Hermitian matrix K_v^sing on endpoint pair-incidence tensors.
For b_{u,v}=sum_i u_i Z_{i,v}, the endpoint contribution is prefactor times b_{u,v}^*K_v^sing b_{u,v}. The spectral theorem gives the lower bound by -Lambda_-(K_v^sing)||b_{u,v}||^2.
Compare the resulting endpoint deficit with M_G. This is a valid regulator-level promotion/falsifier test and does not restate the earlier hairpin threshold.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The finite-dimensional reduction is valid, but the continuum passage still needs uniform bounds showing the endpoint negative spectrum and tail remain below the positive Schur-Feshbach margin without adding boundary renormalization.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Post-H,K endpoint kappa_4 spectral bound for reflected Wilson collars

assumptions: Gauge group is SU(N), tr_F(T^a T^b)=T_F delta^{ab}, and d_A=N^2-1.
The regulator scale satisfies a << rho << ell_min, where ell_min is the smallest non-endpoint geometric separation in the hairpin block.
Heat-kernel plaquette-sheet Wilson observables are reflection-positive at fixed cutoff and admit uniform local cumulant bounds in endpoint boxes.
The Wick-square contraction has already been separated as a positive Gram contribution.
The straight-segment C_A f f commutator contact cancels against the null incidence density for the concrete hairpin geometry.
The remaining non-endpoint OPE tail has a Holder remainder bound with exponent eta>0.
definitions: source object: heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulated reflected Wilson collar block, with endpoint boxes B_v(rho) and parallel transported curvature flux insertions Phi_{v,alpha}^a.
target object: a lower bound for the post-H,K Schur-Feshbach null scalar E_u in terms of the negative spectrum of K_v^sing.
controlled interface: replace each connected boundary-OPE polarization R_ij by its endpoint cumulant matrix plus a tail controlled by OPE Holder regularity.

same-theory condition: the Wilson loops, collar limiting order, heat-kernel normalization, and endpoint parallel transports are fixed before taking the continuum limit; no boundary counterterm or pair-dependent renormalization is inserted.
K_v^sing is the irreducible singlet-projected connected four-flux cumulant after Wick-square and straight f f contact pieces are removed.
Z_{i,v}^{alpha beta} is the endpoint pair-incidence tensor determined by the two plaquette-sheet legs of Wilson observable i at endpoint v.
Lambda_-(A)=max(0,-lambda_min(A)) on the endpoint pair-incidence subspace.

equations.label: endpoint_flux_variable
equations.valid_when: Valid when heat-kernel smearing radius rho is larger than the lattice spacing and smaller than the nearest geometric separation.

equations.label: singlet_endpoint_cumulant
equations.valid_when: Applies after all Wick-square contractions and one-body Wilson normalizations have been subtracted in the same regulator.

equations.label: endpoint_R_matrix
equations.valid_when: Valid when reflected Wilson surfaces are expanded to four endpoint flux insertions with identical plaquette-sheet smearing.

equations.label: null_incidence_norm
equations.valid_when: Valid when u is the Schur-Feshbach null vector and the endpoint pair basis is heat-kernel normalized.

equations.label: negative_spectrum_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when Lambda_- is computed on the finite endpoint incidence subspace after the straight-contact cancellation.

equations.label: tail_bound
equations.valid_when: Requires the regulated connected four-flux density to have an eta-Holder OPE remainder away from endpoint boxes.

equations.label: promotion_inequality
equations.valid_when: Applies after diagonal normalization, Wick-square positivity, and straight f f incidence cancellation have all been verified.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A stable estimate with prefactor times sum_v Lambda_- I_v plus T_tail at least M_G gives a concrete falsifier of same-theory OS positivity for this block.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma converts the remaining R problem into a finite endpoint-box eigenvalue computation with a regulator-level formula and a clear size test.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For the first three-hairpin Schur-Feshbach null channel, the remaining connected boundary-OPE polarization is bounded by the negative spectrum of the singlet heat-kernel endpoint four-flux cumulant plus a controlled tail. If this endpoint deficit is smaller than the positive Gaussian margin M_G, the block passes; if it exceeds M_G stably, it is a same-theory falsifier.

assumptions: The source coupling is gauge-covariant through the same parallel transports used in the Wilson collar observable.
The finite lattice heat-kernel action is analytic for small endpoint sources.
The endpoint box is chosen before the collar limit so the extraction is uniform in the reflected separation.
definitions: Endpoint source J_{v,alpha}^a couples linearly to the smeared transported plaquette curvature Phi_{v,alpha}^a.
The finite endpoint matrix is indexed by unordered plaquette-sheet leg pairs alpha beta at a single reflected hairpin endpoint.
The subtraction removes Wick-square Gram terms and the straight C_A f f contact, leaving the irreducible kappa_4 input.

equations.label: source_partition_function
equations.valid_when: Valid when endpoint sources are inserted only in gauge-covariantly transported plaquette-sheet flux variables.

equations.label: four_source_derivative
equations.latex: \mathcal K^{\rm sing}_{v,\alpha\beta;\gamma\delta}=d_A^{-2}\delta_{ab}\delta_{cd}\,\partial_{J_{v,\alpha}^a}\partial_{J_{v,\beta}^b}\partial_{J_{v,\gamma}^c}\partial_{J_{v,\delta}^d}\log Z_{a,L}(J)|_{J=0}-\mathcal K^{\rm Wick}-\mathcal K^{ff,{\rm str}}
equations.valid_when: Applies at fixed cutoff before continuum extrapolation and after using the same subtraction convention in every matrix entry.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the derivative matrix is regulator-dependent in a way not absorbed by the locked Wilson normalization, the same-theory condition fails before the spectral test is meaningful.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This supplies the next calculational recipe: enumerate endpoint plaquette sources, compute the finite derivative matrix, project to the incidence subspace, and diagonalize.
candidate_lemmas.statement: K_v^sing can be extracted at fixed cutoff by differentiating the logarithm of the heat-kernel lattice partition function with respect to four endpoint plaquette-sheet sources, then projecting the color singlet and subtracting the already-cancelled pieces.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot or quarantine if K_v^sing needs a boundary counterterm, if straight f f cancellation fails with transported orientations, or if the endpoint deficit stably exceeds M_G.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if source differentiation and tail estimates give (g_rho^4/4)(T_F/N)^2 sum_v Lambda_-(K_v^sing)I_v plus T_tail strictly below M_G along the regulator sequence.
control_decision.reason: The branch is not looping: it has replaced the symbolic R entry by a finite heat-kernel endpoint cumulant matrix and a valid negative-spectrum bound.

dependency_updates.description: The locked Wilson algebra must include the heat-kernel plaquette-sheet approximation and the endpoint parallel-transport convention used to define Phi_{v,alpha}.
Continuum convergence must control finite endpoint source derivatives of log Z and not only ordinary Wilson expectation values.
The remaining bridge obligation is now an endpoint-box kappa_4 bound plus an OPE tail estimate after the safe Wick and straight-contact cancellations.

falsifiers: A direct source-derivative computation gives a stable negative endpoint eigenvalue whose prefactor times I_v exceeds M_G; this is the main falsifier.
The straight C_A f f contact fails to cancel after parallel-transport orientation is included, creating a non-endpoint negative term.
The endpoint tail is not O((rho/ell_min)^eta) and remains comparable to the Gaussian margin in the collar limit.
K_v^sing requires a pair-dependent boundary subtraction to have a continuum limit, violating the same-theory condition.
The heat-kernel source extraction is not valid for the locked Wilson algebra because the plaquette-sheet approximation changes the reflected observable family.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 247 turns the post-H,K R term into a concrete finite spectral computation. The actual Yang-Mills object is the singlet source derivative K_v^sing of the heat-kernel plaquette-sheet partition function. Wick-square terms are positive, straight f f contacts cancel by null incidence, and only the negative endpoint kappa_4 spectrum plus a Holder tail can demote the block. This is a valid contribution-making move because it gives the exact regulator matrix to compute and the sign/size inequality needed for promotion or falsifier status.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: At fixed lattice spacing, insert four endpoint plaquette-sheet sources in the heat-kernel action, differentiate log Z, project with d_A^{-2}delta_ab delta_cd, subtract Wick and straight f f pieces, diagonalize K_v^sing on the incidence subspace, and track Lambda_- under two regulator refinements.
